codeReview.summary: The implementation correctly removes the closure-based horizontal()/vertical() layout methods from UiContext, establishing the begin/end style (begin_row/end_row, begin_column/end_column, begin_grid/end_grid) as the sole layout API. The change is confined to a single file (katla_ui/src/context/layout.rs) with -81 lines removed and +7 lines added. Module-level documentation was updated to clearly document the begin/end pattern as primary. Doc comments on begin_row() and begin_column() were updated to remove references to the removed closure methods as 'alternatives'. The retained begin/end methods use safe if-let patterns rather than unwrap() for stack pops.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The SKILL.md for ui-worker contains an example handoff that shows the OPPOSITE decision being made (removing begin/end in favor of closure-based horizontal/vertical). This is misleading for future workers. The example should be updated to reflect the actual decision that was made in this mission.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: SKILL.md example handoff says: 'Removed begin_row/end_row layout style in favor of closure-based horizontal/vertical' — but the actual implementation did the reverse: removed closure-based in favor of begin/end.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The SKILL.md for ui-worker references 'horizontal/vertical closures, begin_row/end_row' in its 'Understand Existing Code' section, implying both still exist. Since this feature removed the closure-based style, the skill file should be updated to reflect only the begin/end pattern exists.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: SKILL.md section 2 says: 'katla_ui/src/context/layout.rs — layout system (horizontal/vertical closures, begin_row/end_row)'

summary: The ui-layout-consistency feature (VAL-UI-001) is correctly implemented. The worker chose the begin/end style as primary since all 12 consumer call sites in katla_app already used it exclusively. The closure-based horizontal()/vertical() methods were cleanly removed from layout.rs with proper documentation updates. No consumers needed changes. The workspace compiles cleanly, and the code follows project conventions.
